gates.title: App identity: icon and name
gates.acceptance: Read the Expo icon field (optional extra.rnqnx.icon override), reject any source that is not a square PNG of at least 1024×1024 in prepare-native and doctor, generate the size set each target needs at build time, listed in the docs, and hash it into native-app.json, and apply it to the launcher tile, title bar, task switcher and QGuiApplication::setWindowIcon (Marathon: app manifest). Ship a default template icon and use it, with a one-line notice naming expo.icon, when no icon is configured; every prepared app gets a generated icon set, prepare-native builds the host identity tool when it is missing and fails on hosts where it cannot be built, and no path ships the platform's blank default icon; never bake corner masks. Enforce tile-name fit by measured rendered width in the launcher font, where the tile label is extra.rnqnx.shortName when set and expo.name otherwise, and expo.name stays the title bar and About name; record the measured label box (width, font, size, line count) for each target launcher; fail with the measured overflow instead of truncating; keep the label single-line with elision. Tests cover longest fitting name, one glyph over, wide glyphs, CJK, emoji and RTL. Host and device receipts show the custom icon in every location and a tile grid where a maximum-length name and a short name produce identical tile sizes.

gates.title: Window chrome and windows API
gates.acceptance: A native QML title bar outside the Fabric root (icon, title, minimize, close; maximize if the target supports it) with macos and windows control layouts selectable in config and at runtime, titleBarStyle default/hidden/none, and a title bar inset exposed to JavaScript and SafeAreaView. Drag-move and edge resize use QWindow::startSystemMove and startSystemResize only where the QPA plugin is verified to support them, with a receipt per target naming each as supported or unsupported. A test or receipt shows the inset values reaching JavaScript. An ADR in docs/adr defines minimize on QNX Screen. A Nitro v1 HybridClass windows API covers title, size, position, minimize, close, close guards, focus and visibility events, and states multi-window scope. Controls are keyboard operable with visible focus and finger-sized hit targets. Device receipts show both layouts, minimize and restore with the AppState transition logged, a close guard that cancels and one that proceeds, and chrome still operable while the JS thread is deliberately blocked.

gates.title: Expo readiness
gates.acceptance: One-command create and an add-to-existing-Expo-app path; static app.json and dynamic app.config.js/.ts resolved through @expo/config; packages/expo-qnx-config-plugins as the single source of native configuration (name, short name, icon, chrome layout, title bar style, initial window size) with no hand-edited native files, and a second prebuild run that changes nothing; Expo CLI owning Metro, logs and reload; a prebuilt development runner, versioned against its SDP, Qt and React Native and verified against a published hash on download, for the QNX release board and for macOS and Linux hosts, a custom development build and a standalone package; a native-module requirement check before JavaScript loads; autolinking of Expo and Nitro modules outside this checkout; a committed Expo SDK 58 package support list generated from tests, with a check that fails when it drifts; apps/expo-router-example running on device. Acceptance: on a clean host without the SDP, create an app, change name, icon and chrome layout only through Expo config and run it on the device in the downloaded runner with Fast Refresh; then with the SDP build and launch the standalone package on the device, recorded end to end.
